title: Biblical Overlap Mining — Wave 23 Next Leads: Rooted Gratitude, Breaking and Experiential Knowing
status: research leads awaiting full dossier promotion

leads.project_wording: We grow the soul in gratitude, and growing a soul is like growing a potato.
leads.possible_structure: rooted → built up → established → abounding in thanksgiving; body supplied/knit together → grows with God's growth
leads.reason: Colossians unusually places rooted growth and thanksgiving inside one sentence, making this more than a generic gratitude comparison.
leads.boundary: Colossians grounds growth in Christ and faith; Potato growth is a modern philosophical analogy and should not replace that role distribution.

leads.possible_structure: fragile vessel/broken container can reveal carried light; death/breaking can disclose distributed life rather than simple annihilation
leads.reason: The project already formalizes breaking→Many/One continuity. Judges' broken jars revealing torches and Paul's treasure-in-earthen-vessels/death-life grammar may provide a useful but carefully separated vessel layer.
leads.boundary: Gideon's jars are a battle tactic and 2 Corinthians concerns apostolic suffering; neither text teaches the Potato book's general law that breaking always reveals wholeness.

leads.project_wording: A potato has no flavor until you chew on it.
leads.possible_structure: truth/goodness is not exhausted by abstract possession; tasting/practice/formed senses produce experiential discernment
leads.reason: The line is comic but carries a real epistemic distinction already explicit on the philosophy page: information present is not the same as understanding assimilated.
leads.boundary: Psalm 34's ‘taste and see’ concerns experiencing Yahweh's goodness; chewing a Potato is a modern comic epistemic metaphor, not a scriptural quotation.
